findings.evidence: Parent commit `e87affbc1492220219f72400b234b0be23102bf1` bootstraps runaway system tables without a `rule` column (e.g. `CreateRunawayWatchTable` / `CreateRunawayTable` in `pkg/session/bootstrap.go`), while `currentBootstrapVersion` is already `version214`. This commit adds `rule VARCHAR(512) DEFAULT ''` to the CREATE TABLE definitions and adds `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN rule` inside `upgradeToVer212` (`pkg/session/bootstrap.go`), but does not bump `currentBootstrapVersion` (still `version214`). As a result, a cluster already bootstrapped/upgraded to bootstrap version 214 on the parent commit will not run any upgrade when starting this commit’s binary (upgrade short-circuits when `ver >= currentBootstrapVersion`). Meanwhile runtime SQL paths now expect the new column (e.g. `INSERT INTO mysql.tidb_runaway_queries (..., rule, ...)` in `pkg/resourcegroup/runaway/record.go`).
findings.fix: Bump bootstrap version (add `version215`, set `currentBootstrapVersion = version215`) and add an `upgradeToVer215` that adds the `rule` column to `mysql.tidb_runaway_watch`, `mysql.tidb_runaway_watch_done`, and `mysql.tidb_runaway_queries` using reentrant DDL (ignore `ErrColumnExists`). Do not rely on `upgradeToVer212` for clusters already at 214 because it won’t run when upgrading from 214→214.
findings.impact: Upgrade/rolling-forward from a build at the first-parent commit (bootstrap version already recorded as 214) can leave the three runaway system tables without the new `rule` column, causing user-visible runtime failures when runaway/query-watch functionality reads or writes these tables (e.g. `Unknown column 'rule'` / `Column count doesn't match value count`), and potentially breaking `information_schema.runaway_watches`/runaway sync/flush workflows.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master`: the only `ADD COLUMN `rule`` DDL for runaway tables remains tied to the version-212 upgrade logic (`pkg/session/upgrade_def.go` `upgradeToVer212`), with no later-version upgrade step that would backfill `rule` for clusters that already recorded bootstrap version >=214 without the column.
findings.verify: Simulate/confirm on a cluster bootstrapped with parent `e87affbc...` (bootstrap ver=214) then start a binary containing the fix: `SHOW COLUMNS FROM mysql.tidb_runaway_watch LIKE 'rule';` (and the other two tables) should return a row; then execute a minimal flow that inserts runaway/watch records (or directly run the internal insert SQL) and ensure it succeeds; query `information_schema.runaway_watches` and confirm the `RULE` column is populated/non-erroring.
findings.what: System-table schema upgrade gap: adds `rule` column to runaway tables without bumping bootstrap version, so clusters already at `version214` on the parent commit won’t auto-upgrade and will be left with a schema that the new runtime SQL expects.
